In simple_ddl_parser/ddl_parser.py the lexer rule t_DOT = r"." matches any character, so characters with no lexer rule (such as backticks) are silently turned into DOT tokens instead of raising an error.
quote: The backtick is being lexed as a `DOT` token because `t_DOT = r"."` matches any character in regex.

statement: PLY, the lexer library this parser uses, tries function-based token rules in the order they appear in the source file (by line number), so where a new t_* function is placed in ddl_parser.py decides which rule matches first.
quote: PLY sorts function rules by line number.

statement: DDLParser hides parse errors (p_error just passes), so a DDL statement that fails to parse makes run() return an empty list [] instead of raising an exception. To debug, feed the input to the lexer directly (parser.lexer.input / token()) and inspect the tokens it produces.
